static_traits.name: Zhu Liya
static_traits.social_status: A few friends to confide in, but relationship tension from constantly seeking reassurance about the band's news, affecting communication
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness, never received psychotherapy or mental health services before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, capable of self-reflection, high cooperativeness; tense but positive emotional attitude, good narrative logic

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am a terrible fan, believing my favorite band Nightfish's breakup was caused by my negative thoughts and behavior, so I blame and guilt myself daily for it, with worsening anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to participate in serious conversations and take responsibility better; I also want to stop using humor as a crutch and feel more fulfilled.
growth_experiences: Since adolescence she began using humor to ease anxiety under pressure or in important situations, a pattern of avoiding evaluation; this coping style continues to this day, increasingly evident recently in work meetings and roommate interactions, leading others to see her as not serious enough, making deeper connection hard.

core_beliefs: My negative thoughts and behavior will cause bad things to happen

special_situations.event: Hearing rumors that Nightfish might disband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have negative thoughts or do not-good-enough things as a fan, the band will be affected or even break up
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Non-stop searching for information and verification online, monitoring news to try to prevent bad things from happening
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I made them break up

special_situations.event: Band members hinting at tension in social media or interviews
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If tension signs appear, it means a breakup is unavoidable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling attention to news and updates, refreshing repeatedly to confirm they are not breaking up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will definitely fall apart and disband soon

special_situations.event: When listening to Nightfish's music or reading related news
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good fans should not have negative thoughts; if I follow them while having negative thoughts, it means I am a bad fan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labels herself an 'I am a bad fan' and blames herself, trying to use guilt to urge herself to 'correct' it
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a terrible fan, nothing I do is good

special_situations.event: Feeling anxious in important work meetings, worried about being evaluated by others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not tell jokes and speak seriously, everyone will think I am incompetent, or saying the wrong thing will be mocked
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using humor to deflect attention, avoiding expressing serious views to escape possible evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will find me unprofessional, and if I speak seriously I will surely embarrass myself

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted and affirmed by others, to be taken seriously and seen as a 'good fan/good colleague'
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of negative evaluation, of being blamed for causing bad outcomes for others or the group (such as the band breaking up)
defense_goal: Keeping a safe distance through humor to avoid others' judgment
Gaining a sense of control through excessive research and verification, lowering uncertainty and anxiety
Maintaining 'control' over the situation through self-blame and guilt, trying to make up for anxiety

object_relations.object_representation: A band that is fragile, easily affected by self, and may fall apart at any time

object_relations.self_representation: A colleague easily questioned, not taken seriously
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges (colleagues / supervisors) who may negate her at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor guides into more serious/more emotional topics or asks to concretely explore responsibility and contribution
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Without humor to protect herself, she will be judged on the spot or exposed as 'incompetent'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a light joking tone, deflecting to unrelated light topics, reducing emotional expression and eye contact.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about feelings and inner experience, while external information is uncertain (like conflicting rumors and clues)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing all facts and data must be clarified first, or expressing feelings would seem unreliable or be negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Answers by listing information and deducing from data, reducing subjective emotional words, with a calm, analytical tone.

manifestations: Takes excessive personal responsibility for external events (whether the band breaks up)
Treats others' evaluations as important references; fears negative judgment
Avoiding real expression and choice through humor, lowering anxiety about freedom and responsibility
outcomes: Decline in work performance and interpersonal alienation

manifestations: Living alone and hard to bare true beliefs and worries to friends
Uses jokes to maintain superficial interaction, reduces real contact
outcomes: Reduced sense of relational connection, superficial experience
Support system hard to use effectively
Restricted emotional experience, increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Deflecting attention by joking in serious topics or important meetings
Dissolving discomfort with humor in counseling, reducing direct emotional confrontation
Quickly switching to light topics when talking about anxiety

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming others see her as incompetent or will mock her
Attributing possible negative evaluation to others' intentions (like colleagues / supervisors not taking her seriously)

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently blaming oneself as a 'bad fan', rigid self-demands
Over-reviewing and restraining before expressing views, worried about being negated

positive_force: High self-awareness; can clearly describe problem patterns and impacts
Positive attitude, willing to try new ways of contact and behavioral experiments
Has a certain degree of social support (a few friends) and a stable life structure (working from home, caring for pets)
negative_force: Excessive personalized attribution and self-blame (blaming external events on oneself)
Catastrophizing and jumping to conclusions (negative anticipation about the band's news)
Continuous online verification and excessive research maintaining anxiety and uncertainty
Highly sensitive to others' evaluations, using humor to avoid real contact, hindering effective communication

target_behavior.behavior: Over-researches band dynamics and repeatedly seeks reassurance online
antecedent: Hearing rumors that Nightfish might disband
Sees messages or posts from members hinting at tense relationships
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizing external events, trying to ease uncertainty and anxiety through information control
target_behavior.function: Escaping anxiety from uncertainty, gaining brief security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety maintained and intensified, work and daily life (reading, caring for the pet) disrupted

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding serious expression and responsibility with humor in serious settings
antecedent: Important meetings or task assignments at work
Situations requiring serious communication with roommates or others
Occasions where one feels about to be evaluated or might 'say the wrong thing'
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of negative evaluation and seeming incompetent, using humor as a defensive and avoidant strategy
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential shame and judgment, lowering present anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Seen as not serious enough, affecting work performance and trust; interpersonal connections staying superficial, hard to deepen

target_behavior.behavior: Daily self-blaming and guilty self-talk repeated
antecedent: Reading information related to the band
Recalling, associating rumors or signs of tension
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am a bad fan' and 'my negative thoughts will cause bad things' triggers self-labeling and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Gaining the illusion of 'making up' and control through self-blame, trying to lower anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Intensified emotional pain (anxiety, shame, guilt), impaired attention and functional decline (work, interpersonal, daily)
